title: Informal Conjecture (vertex-disjoint paths, stability number two)
statement_text: We suspect the $k$ vertex-disjoint paths problem might be NP-complete for digraphs with stability number two.
context_text: Digraphs are finite, without loops or parallel edges, but may have both edges $uv$ and $vu$; paths are directed. Given distinct vertices $s_1,t_1,\dots,s_k,t_k$ of a digraph $G$, the $k$ vertex-disjoint paths problem asks whether there are pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths $P_1,\dots,P_k$ with $P_i$ from $s_i$ to $t_i$. A set of vertices is stable if no edge has both ends in it, and the stability number is the size of a largest stable set; a digraph is semicomplete if for all distinct $u,v$ at least one of $uv,vu$ is an edge (so semicomplete digraphs are exactly those of stability number one). The problem is NP-complete in general digraphs even for $k=2$ (Fortune, Hopcroft and Wyllie), and NP-complete for tournaments when $k$ is not fixed (Bang-Jensen and Thomassen); the authors had earlier shown it is polynomial-time solvable for every fixed $k$ on semicomplete digraphs, and here extend this to digraphs whose vertex set is given partitioned into a bounded number of sets each inducing a semicomplete digraph. A natural further extension would be to digraphs of bounded stability number: the edge-disjoint version is polynomial-time solvable there, but the vertex-disjoint version remains out of reach, and the authors suspect that it might already be NP-complete for stability number two (the paper does not say explicitly whether $k$ is meant to be fixed, but the discussion concerns extending the fixed-$k$ result).
